verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev's docs and llms.txt describe it as an "open source" framework and platform, and there is a public GitHub repository at triggerdotdev/trigger.dev; self-hosting docs further indicate the platform code is available to run yourself. missing for 10: explicit identification of the specific license (e.g., Apache-2.0/MIT) in evidence, independent or hands-on corroboration that the full platform source (not just the SDK) is published under that license.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Trigger.dev is an open source background jobs framework that lets you write reliable workflows in plain async code.
Open source platform for durable, long-running tasks.
Build rock solid agents and AI applications using our durable tasks, retries, queues and idempotency.
Self-hosting Trigger.dev means you run and manage the platform on your own infrastructure
